thread:
aina: heads up — I'm opening a short RFC follow-up: proposal to add a "reslicing" layer in the prefetch coordinator that can dynamically reshuffle shard windows to reduce memory blowups during warmup. TLDR: allows smaller contiguous reads + opportunistic merge when needed.

mike: concrete problem we're solving?

aina: spikes in OOM during concurrent model loads when large shards are hot. current options: big contiguous mmap reads or many tiny reads — either OOM or perf cliff. reslicing would pick mid-sized windows and stitch them to satisfy both.

sophia: sounds like hybrid prefetch. how does this interact with safetensors index-first vs streaming?

aina: index-first stays same — reslicing operates at transport/loader layer. for manifestless streaming we maintain a lightweight reassembly map so readers see contiguous weight ranges. no change to safetensors payload.

raj: how do we expose this in the loader API? we don't want to leak complexity to runtime callers.

aina: proposal: add a PrefetchHint enum to the weightsource API: {FAST_CONTIGUOUS, BALANCED_RESLICED, ON_DEMAND}. default BALANCED for heavy models. loader decides actual windowing. callers can opt-in for FAST_CONTIGUOUS when latency-critical.

mike: do we change shard placement logic? e.g., reslicing across shard boundaries could cross network calls.

aina: we restrict reslicing to within a checkpoint "bundle" (same transport host/URL). cross-host merges are allowed only as fallback and async post-warmup to avoid extra p99.

loader-bot: automated test run queued for reslice-prototype (CI #4213).

raj: eviction/priority implications? if we prefetch many mid-windows, eviction becomes harder. we should add a soft-lease or window-priority metric.

aina: agreed — plan includes WindowLease with credit accounting. windows consumed by active inferences get higher priority; stale windows are evictable.

sophia: how do we ensure correctness with KV cache indexing? offsets must be stable for attention table mapping.

aina: reslicer will present a virtual contiguous view to the runtime. we maintain offset translation table (tiny) that maps virtual offsets -> underlying window descriptors. KV cache deals with virtual offsets only.

mike: translation table size worst-case? if we slice heavily across many tiny windows it could grow.

aina: cap windows per layer/parameter to a small N (default 8). if model demands more, fall back to contiguous read for that param.

raj: metrics we should add: reslice-hit, windows-per-param histogram, window-merge-duration, extra-reads-per-warmup.

aina: yes + regression alerts in Console when reslice increases p95 tokens or cold-start time.

sophia: compatibility with quantized/packed formats? e.g., 4-bit packed requires bit-aligned reads.

aina: allocator supports bitrange mapping; reslicing must respect packing boundaries. we'll detect format and only allow window splits at pack boundaries. fall back otherwise.

mike: rollout plan? feature flag?

aina: feature-flagged in Dedicated/private for an A/B canary. start with small models then scale. docs + quick CLI:

```
redwoodctl loader set-prefetch --model t5-large --policy BALANCED_RESLICED
```

ajnote: loader-bot says CI passed for small-scale tests.

raj: edgecases: partial checksum validation if windows arrive out of order. we need per-window checksums ala sidecar manifest.

aina: yep — window manifests with per-window checksum + sequence id. streaming path includes minimal header. No protocol break for existing manifests.

mike: any perf numbers?

aina: prototype on dev rig: for 8B model cold-start memory peak reduced ~22% and warmup latency up 8% avg but P95 reduced in constrained mem env. willing to trade a bit of avg latency for stability.

sophia: +1 for default BALANCED. minor nit: name "reslice" might confuse future maintainers. suggest "windowed-prefetch" or "microwindow".

aina: noted. open to renaming.

raj: next steps? PR, perf harness, and an eng-ml design review.

aina: I'll draft PR with design doc and a simple state diagram. will ping @eng-ml for review. thanks all. :rocket:
